title: Radioactive decay law
references: Rutherford, E. and Soddy, F., The cause and nature of radioactivity, Part I, Philosophical Magazine 4(21), 370-396 (1902), doi:10.1080/14786440209462856
Krane, K. S., Introductory Nuclear Physics, 3rd ed., Wiley (1988)
validity_domain: Expected number N(t) = N0 exp(-t ln2 / T_half) of undecayed nuclei of one isotope after a time t, from N0 nuclei at t = 0.
limitations: Statistical law: an actual count fluctuates around the expected value (about the square root of N for a Poisson process), so a small sample can lie outside the 1 % band without a contradiction
The half-life is a parameter of the isotope, it is not provided by the law and is never assumed
Single isotope with no feeding from a parent: decay chains need the Bateman equations
Time units are s, min, h and d; a half-life in years must be converted by the user
Holds for a constant decay probability per unit time, which is the case for ordinary decay modes of free nuclei
